knowledge_point.title: Finding a Point on a Line That Is Closest to a Given Point

question.:question/problem:
![](images/c0/c0e534ede9457e7642697eea0b1f5b4e18454c69e233fb53570181538341fdb0.png)

Find the point on the line $y=-\frac{2 x}{3} -6$ that is closest to the point $(2,-3).$
question.:question/worked-solution:
First, we find the equation of the line that's perpendicular to $y=-\frac{2 x}{3} -6$ and passes through the point $(2,-3).$

The given line has a slope of $-\frac{2}{3},$ so our perpendicular line must have a slope of $\frac{3}{2}.$

Using point-slope form and simplifying, we obtain the equation of the perpendicular line:

$$
\begin{aligned}y-y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y-(-3) &= \frac{3}{2}(x-(2)) \\ y-(-3) &= \frac{3 x}{2} -3 \\ y &= \frac{3 x}{2} -6\end{aligned}
$$

We now find the point where the two lines intersect. To do this, we solve the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{cases}y=-\frac{2 x}{3} -6 \\ y=\frac{3 x}{2} -6\end{cases}
$$

We can solve this system by putting the two equations equal to one another and solving for $x.$ This gives

$$
\begin{aligned}-\frac{2 x}{3} -6 &= \frac{3 x}{2} -6 \\ -\frac{13 x}{6} &= 0 \\ x &= 0\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting $x=0$ into either of the two equations gives $y=-6.$ So, our solution is $x=0$ and $y=-6.$ Therefore, the lines intersect at the point $(0,-6).$

Therefore, we conclude that the point on the line $y=-\frac{2 x}{3} -6$ that is closest to the point $(2,-3)$ is $(0,-6).$
